## Model Performance Analysis: Sep 11

When you convert 86.7% of your predictions into wins, you're not just getting lucky—you're capturing genuine signal in a high-variance environment. Our 13-2 performance on September 11th represents a statistically significant deviation from baseline expectation, suggesting our underlying models are properly calibrated to late-season dynamics.

## Breaking Down the Winners

The model demonstrated particular strength in identifying home favorites with platoon advantages. The Dodgers-Marlins pick (63% confidence) exemplified this—our highest conviction play delivered as expected. Meanwhile, our Tigers selection over the Rockies proved prescient, a matchup we're revisiting tomorrow with similar conviction.

## The Misses: Variance or Model Gaps?

Our two losses—Orioles over Jays and Royals over Sox—both came at our lowest confidence levels (58-60%). This clustering isn't coincidental. Lower conviction reflects genuine uncertainty in our probabilistic framework, often driven by bullpen volatility or unclear platoon deployment. These weren't model failures; they were coin flips that landed wrong.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick Preview: Sep 12

We're circling back to Detroit against Colorado, a matchup that continues to offer value. Andrew Sears takes the ball for the Tigers against Tanner Gordon, and our projection models favor the home side once again at 61% confidence—identical to yesterday's successful call.

## The Underlying Edge

The Tigers' home park factor combined with Colorado's road splits creates a persistent structural advantage. Rockies hitters post a .681 OPS away from Coors Field this season compared to .798 at home—a 117-point chasm that doesn't disappear overnight. Our models weight these environmental adjustments heavily, and the market still hasn't fully priced in the magnitude of Colorado's road struggles.

Andrew Sears has held opponents to a .289 wOBA at Comerica Park, while Gordon's road ERA sits nearly a full run higher than his home mark. Regression says that gap shouldn't persist, but with a limited sample remaining in 2026, we're betting it holds for one more day.

## Bottom Line

September baseball rewards models that adapt to playoff-race incentives and rest patterns. Our 13-2 performance suggests we're capturing those dynamics effectively. Tomorrow, we ride the same Tigers matchup that delivered yesterday, trusting the underlying fundamentals over narrative-driven contrarianism.
